_doc: Dangerous variable defaults that are KNOWN — read by scripts/check-tfvars-safety.mjs.
TWO KINDS, because a default is dangerous in two directions. An entry's "kind" field says
which; an entry with no "kind" means "empty-default", the original one, so every pre-#3292
entry keeps its meaning unchanged.
· "empty-default" (#3108) — the default is ABSENT ("", [], {}, false, null) and it reaches a
count/for_each gate or steers a conditional. The unset value silently decides.
· "permissive-default" (#3292) — the default is PRESENT and OPEN: an access-control variable
whose default carries a CIDR with prefix length 0, i.e. the whole address space. Nothing
is silent about it — it is simply the allowlist that gets applied.
The kind is part of the key. "This list is deliberately empty" and "this list is deliberately
open" are opposite claims, and an entry making one must not absolve the other: narrowing an
open default to [] must make the permissive entry go STALE and fail, not quietly carry over.
WHAT AN ENTRY MEANS. Someone looked at this (stack, variable) pair and wrote down what taking
the default costs. It does not mean the default is right; several entries below say the
opposite and name the issue that will decide. It means the decision is recorded rather than
discovered during an apply.
WHY A BASELINE AND NOT AN EXEMPTION LIST. #3108 found 36 sites across 21 stacks. Fixing all of
them in one change would mean committing values nobody has checked against a live account,
which is the failure #3105 was written to prevent, not a fix for it. So the guard ratchets: a
NEW empty default reaching a decision fails immediately, and the backlog is visible and
shrinking rather than implicit.
THE KEY IS (stack, variable), NOT file:line. A line number drifts on any edit above it, and the
decision belongs to the variable — so an entry covers every site in that stack which reads it.
A STALE ENTRY FAILS. When a variable stops being a finding — its input gets committed, or it
becomes REQUIRED — this entry no longer describes anything and the check says so. Remove it in
the PR that fixed it; that diff is the review. A baseline that outlives what it describes is
how a ratchet goes slack, and it leaves the next person adding the same defect pre-forgiven.
NOT IN HERE, because they were fixed rather than recorded: aws-oidc (#3105) and, in #3108,
github, gcp-e2e, azure-e2e and alibaba-e2e.

known.reason: [] makes the 'the e2e region must not be a prod region' check (checks.tf:101) vacuously true — a safety check satisfied by the absence of its own input. Deliberate for now: there is no Alibaba production estate for an e2e region to collide with. The moment one exists this must be filled in, and the check starts meaning something.

[] removes the AdminAssume statement from the deploy-role and e2e-nightly trust policies (main.tf:65, e2e-nightly.tf:92). It narrows to OIDC-only, which is the SAFE direction — but it silently removes a human break-glass path, and re-adding it later is an IAM change. Deliberate: nobody should hold standing assume rights on these roles.

"" falls back to a data lookup of the account's existing GitHub OIDC provider (main.tf:20) rather than gating anything. Benign, and the fallback is the intended path — the variable exists to override it in an account where the provider is named unusually.

"" drops the sts:ExternalId confused-deputy condition from the cross-account trust (main.tf:59), leaving the ArnLike aws:PrincipalArn condition alone. Stays optional on purpose: this stack MIRRORS the connector's own optional external_id field, and requiring it here would test something the product does not require. What it must not be is silent, so checks.tf now carries `external_id_is_a_decision_not_a_default`, which says on every plan that the control is absent.

THE INVERSION, and the sharpest finding in the sweep: main.tf:66 reads `default_action = length(...) > 0 ? "Deny" : "Allow"`, so the UNSET value is the permissive one and the state storage account defaults to network-open. Not decided here — flipping the polarity can lock the maintainer out of their own backend. Filed as #3290.

[] removes every Storage Blob Data Contributor assignment on the state account (main.tf:103). Shared-key auth is disabled there, so with zero assignments every `tofu init` against that backend 403s and the state becomes unreachable. The value is a personal Entra object id, so it cannot be committed to a public repo; main.tf:112-117 already carries a `check` that names the failure and the `az ad signed-in-user show` command that produces the id.
Same shape and same decision as aws-oidc's: [] removes the AdminAssume statement from the alethia-connector-assets-deployer trust (deployer.tf:38). OIDC-only is intended.

false is the deliberate default and the whole point of this bootstrap: the account already has a GitHub OIDC provider (created by aws-oidc), so this stack ADOPTS it via oidc_provider_arn rather than creating a second one. Creating one where another exists is the error, which is why the safe value is the default here and `true` in email-ses/bootstrap.

"" makes the stack auto-select an availability zone from a data source (main.tf:34,48) instead of pinning one. Benign, and intended for a first apply — but it is non-deterministic across applies, so pin it if a zone ever needs to stay put.

false leaves 11 Cloudflare email-routing resources ungated-into-existence (email-routing.tf:39,49,57,81), including the 8 inbound addresses printed in transactional email footers. The ONLY finding in this sweep that CI can trip by itself: infra-cp-hetzner.yml:103 runs `tofu apply -auto-approve` on push to main and nothing sets the variable. Harmless while the state is genuinely empty, which variables.tf:44-47 records; the hazard is the moment those resources exist. Filed as #3291.

["0.0.0.0/0", "::/0"] is the source_ips of the port-22 rule on the alethia-cp firewall (main.tf:33), and infra-cp-hetzner.yml runs `tofu apply -auto-approve` on push to main with nothing supplying a narrower value — so the open default is not a placeholder, it IS the applied production configuration. There IS a recorded reason, quoted from variables.tf:90-91: "GitHub-hosted runner egress IPs are dynamic, so SSH stays open by default (key-only auth). Restrict to a bastion/Tailscale range to harden later." True — the ranges are published but large and they move. Key-only auth is a mitigation, not the control this variable is named after. Whether GitHub's published meta ranges or a bastion/Tailscale hop can replace 0.0.0.0/0 is #3292 point 2, and it is the MAINTAINER's decision: a wrong CIDR here locks CI out of the control-plane box.
Same shape and same decision as aws-oidc's: [] removes the AdminAssume statement from the alethia-ses-deployer trust (deployer.tf:37). OIDC-only is intended.

"" derives the bucket name as alethia-tofu-state-<project_id> (main.tf:27). Benign, and the derivation is the intended path — but it does mean the bucket a bare apply targets is a function of another variable, so a mis-set project_id silently retargets state rather than failing.

["0.0.0.0/0", "::/0"] is the source_ips of the port-22 rule on the sandbox box (network.tf:16). The one of the three #3292 cases that is NOT applied unattended: the maintainer applies this stack by hand and narrows the value in an untracked terraform.tfvars, which this check cannot see and must not assume (terraform.tfvars.example:23 shows the shape, `ssh_allowed_cidrs = ["203.0.113.4/32"]`). Recorded reason, quoted from variables.tf:47-49: "Unlike cp-hetzner (which must accept dynamic GitHub-runner egress), this box is only ever reached from one laptop, so it CAN be locked down. Default is open to keep a first apply from locking you out; narrow it in terraform.tfvars." #3292 point 3 says keep as is — the lock-yourself-out reasoning holds for a first apply, and the value is narrowed in practice.

UNJUSTIFIED. This entry records outstanding DEBT — #3292 point 1 — not an accepted exception, and it is here to be deleted rather than kept. ["0.0.0.0/0", "::/0"] is the source_ips of the port-22 rule on the alethia-status firewall (main.tf:29); infra-status.yml runs `tofu apply -auto-approve` on push to main and no committed tfvars narrows it, so an internet-open SSH allowlist is the live configuration of that box. Unlike infra/cp-hetzner and infra/sandbox, variables.tf:47-51 carries NO reason at all: nobody chose the open value, it is what an unfilled declaration left behind. The issue calls this the actionable half. Baselined ONLY so the guard can go green on the tree as it stands — narrowing it here would be an agent guessing a CIDR for a box CI applies unattended, which is how you lock CI out. The fix is the maintainer's: narrow the default, or write down in variables.tf why it cannot be narrowed, and delete this entry in the same PR.
